title: Console: Tile-weight rebalance + single-span trace preview + compact cost delta rollup
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Context: The Console Observability Revamp PRD initially scoped a broad feature set: full trace explorer, per-route cost attribution, multi-card dashboards with drill-throughs, and token-level cost breakdowns. Team velocity constraints + dependency risks on the serving runtime integration require a surgical MVP cut to guarantee an on-time, usable alpha for internal customers. This ticket defines the reduced-scope surface: 1) 'Lightweight tiles' - single-card KPIs with one-click expand to a compact detail pane; 2) 'Single-span trace preview' - show the highest-latency span with basic metadata and ability to open full trace in External Tracing if available; 3) 'Compact cost delta rollup' - present week-over-week and per-route deltas with a top-five route list and absolute delta numbers rather than a full attribution engine. Purpose: avoid delay from building heavy backends (attribution pipelines, token-level sampling) while enabling product teams to triage performance and cost regressions. This ticket captures scope cuts, acceptance criteria, design constraints, rollout plan, and developer handoff notes.
acceptance_criteria: Lightweight tiles: Dashboard landing shows up to 6 tiles (latency p50/p95, error rate, request rate, cost delta, top-5 routes, recent incidents). Each tile must load within 400ms for an internal test dataset.

Single-span trace preview: From a tile or route list, clicking a 'preview' opens a compact view that displays the single highest-latency span (span name, duration, service, timestamp) and a link/button 'Open full trace' which navigates to external tracing (if linked). No in-console full-span waterfall is required for this MVP.

Compact cost delta rollup: Cost tile computes and displays % and absolute delta for the selected period (7d vs prior 7d) and lists the top 5 routes contributing to the delta. Calculations must match the existing cost-job baseline for the same inputs within 2%.
Design constraints: Tile weight budget of 60kb payload per tile on initial API responses. All tiles must gracefully degrade and show a skeleton or 'data unavailable' when backend data is missing.

Telemetry & metrics: Feature must emit two new counters (console.tile.load, console.trace.preview.open) and a latency histogram for tile render time. These must be wired to the staging observability dashboard before beta.
Rollout: Alpha internal rollout to Redwood engineering + selected beta partners (max 10 orgs) with opt-in flag. No force enable for all customers until GA verification.
Documentation: Quickstart help doc and a short PRD update summarizing cuts and known gaps must be published in Confluence before alpha invite.
QA: All acceptance scenarios must pass manual QA in staging and automated E2E smoke tests must be added to the Console CI pipeline.
decision_log: 2026-02-25: PM wrote PRD v1 with broad scope (full trace explorer + attribution). Engineering flagged dependencies on infra jobs and kernel-level sampling.
2026-02-28: Leadership alignment — choose to prioritize observable triage flows over full-feature completions to meet Q1 alpha milestone.
2026-03-02: Cut accepted: drop token-level cost breakdown, postpone full trace waterfall, remove in-console complex attribution for now. Replace with aggregated rollup + top-5 list.
2026-03-05: Added metric budget (tile payload and render latency) after frontend perf spike during prototype demo.
2026-03-08: Decided to surface 'Open full trace' that redirects to partner tracing UIs instead of building full tracing backend.
Rationale: Minimizes infra work, preserves core triage user journey, and reduces risk of missed deadlines while providing measurable improvements to developer troubleshooting workflows.
progress_updates: 2026-03-03: Kickoff meeting. Attendees: PM (Aisha), Eng Lead (Ravi Shah), FE (Marco Liu), Design (Leah Park). Action: produce page-level wireframes and API contract sketch.
2026-03-04: Design spike completed: low-fidelity tiles and compact trace preview mocks (see design links). Prototype shows render time spikes >600ms; flagged as blocker for FE optimization.
2026-03-06: ENG created API stubs ENG-57890 for cost rollup and ENG-59012 for trace preview link. Backend team estimates 3 sprints to support full attribution if later needed.
2026-03-09: FE implemented skeletons + minimal client to show aggregated tile data. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/6123 (work in progress).
2026-03-10: PM published alpha invite plan and started identifying internal orgs for test.
design_feedback: Design asked to cap tile payload to reduce TTFB and avoid jank on low-end devices. Recommended deferring per-route drilldowns to later iterations.
Requested accessible color contrast updates to the delta visualization; FE to adopt tokens from design system rather than bespoke styles.
Design requested a clear empty-state pattern for when cost data is delayed (use tertiary copy: 'Cost data is processing — check back in ~10 minutes').
dev_notes: Backend: Provide aggregated pre-computed rollups for 7d vs prior 7d keyed by route id. Response should include top_5_routes array of {route_id, name, delta_absolute, delta_percent}.
Frontend: Implement lazy loading — show top-level tiles immediately, fetch expanded details on click. Keep ZIO for concurrent fetch handling to minimize waterfalling.
Perf: Keep client-side processing under 80ms for sorting top routes and rendering compact preview.
Telemetry wiring: Use existing console metrics namespace; add logs for preview open events with org_id and route_id.
If external tracing link is not configured for an org, hide 'Open full trace' button and surface CTA to 'Configure tracing' pointing to org settings.
ENG-57890 and ENG-59012 must be ready in staging before FE beta gating; coordinate daily standups until done.
rollout_plan: Alpha (internal) — 2026-03-18: Feature flag gated; enable for Redwood engineering orgs to validate telemetry and performance.
Beta (external opt-in) — 2026-04-01: Enable for up to 10 partner orgs; collect qualitative feedback and bug reports.
GA criteria — 1) tile render median < 450ms across alpha; 2) no P1 regressions; 3) positive qualitative feedback from at least 3 partners. Target GA: 2026-04-15.
Rollback: Feature flag off; migrate users back to current Console landing flow. Prepare a runbook to revert backend rollup endpoints if unexpected cost deltas reported.
qa_checks: Manual: Validate tile numbers against raw cost job for a sample org; test missing-data flows and skeleton states.
Automated: Add E2E test that asserts presence of 6 tiles and opens trace preview; assert preview contains span name and duration.
Performance: CI job should run a headless render check and fail if median tile load > 600ms on staging data.
Security: Confirm no PII surfaces in trace preview; preview must truncate any user identifiers in span attributes.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Aggregated rollup numbers may differ from long-running attribution jobs leading to customer confusion. Mitigation: add explanatory tooltip 'Compact rollup — not full attribution' and link to docs explaining the gap.
Risk: FE perf may remain above target. Mitigation: reduce tile count to 4 as an emergency cut and postpone cost delta until performance improvements are merged.
Risk: External tracing links vary by partner. Mitigation: detect and hide link when not available, and track missing-tracing telemetry for prioritization.
Risk: Metrics gap for GA sign-off. Mitigation: require telemetry wiring as a prereq for beta enablement; do not opt-in partners until metrics are visible.
